question: The system of equations $x + y + z = 0$, $x + 2y + 3z = 0$, $x + 3y + 6z = 0$ has
explanation:
Write the coefficient matrix of the system.
$A = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 6 \end{vmatrix}$.
Compute the determinant.
$=1\begin{vmatrix}2&3\\3&6\end{vmatrix}-1\begin{vmatrix}1&3\\1&6\end{vmatrix}+1\begin{vmatrix}1&2\\1&3\end{vmatrix}$.
$=1(12-9)-1(6-3)+1(3-2)$.
$=3-3+1$.
$=1$.
Since $|A| \neq 0$, the system has a unique solution.
